title: Lens: web UI architecture
summary: The web UI is a set of thin Server Component routes over 39 client components. There are 22 pages, and only 2 of them load data on the server. Each client component fetches, writes and renders on its own. The screens agree on the lowest layer: every form control comes from components/ui/field, the Luma tokens are imported once, and almost every read response is parsed with a generated validator. Above that layer they share almost nothing. In 23 component files, data is fetched inside effects that keep their own loading and error flags. The CSRF write path appears in 29 call sites across 19 files, with hand-built headers, untyped JSON bodies and, at 19 sites, cast error bodies. Only 8 of those 19 files stop a second press while a request is in flight, and the composer, the session screen and the workflow run are not among them. Loading, error and denied states, refusal texts, run-state words and tones, and money and time formats are each written per screen, and they visibly disagree. Two well-shaped hooks already exist, useLoaded in tool-catalog and useToolUses, and ContinueRun handles an unknown outcome correctly. These show the target patterns, but they stay private to their files. There are two root causes. First, there is no shared layer: no typed browser client, no resource or submit hooks, no view-state components and no lib vocabulary. Second, the generated client drops query parameters and refusal bodies, so screens cannot use it. Building that layer first would let the ten screen functions of 260 to 677 lines split along the same seams, and it would turn most findings below into mechanical migrations.

scores.why: TypeScript is strict, lint passes and every form control comes from ui/field. DH-06's rules on duplicate submits, generated request types and Server Components are met only in part, and type sizes bypass the theme.
The server-only lib boundary is clean. Shared vocabulary and hooks live inside feature components, which import each other sideways with one cycle, and there are no hooks or feature folders.
The ten longest functions are route screens of 260 to 677 lines, with complexity up to 39. Each one mixes data loading, writes and markup.
The pure helpers are small and well named. The screen components interleave effects, writes and rendering, and the same write shape is repeated at 29 call sites.
Routes are thin server pages over one client panel. The 43 feature components sit in one flat folder, recurring layout pieces are private to screens, and the run routes own their own headers.
There is no shared data, submit or view-state layer. 23 files hand-roll fetch effects, live updates and URL state differ per screen, and only two pages load data on the server.
Comments explain why and cite decisions. A few record manual sync duties that a shared module would remove, for example run-workspace.tsx:48 and lib/shortcuts.ts:1-2.

Read responses are parsed with generated validators. 28 request bodies, 19 error-body reads and 7 success-body reads bypass the generated types, and many label maps are keyed by string instead of the generated unions.
Most failures are shown in words. States and announcement roles differ per screen, three loads stay on Loading after a failure, search shows an outage as no results, and refusal texts diverge.
Playwright coverage is broad and uses data-* hooks. Pure UI helpers sit inside client components with no unit tests, and the unit runner names two of the three test files.
The screens are careful and accessible, but their per-screen plumbing turns every cross-cutting change (contracts, states, formatting) into a many-file edit.

strengths.title: Read responses are validated at the browser boundary
strengths.evidence: 25 component files parse responses with generated parse* functions before use, for example run-list.tsx:193, approvals-panel.tsx:143 and tool-uses.tsx:133. Unknown event types are skipped on purpose rather than cast (run-workspace.tsx:143-150). The runtime validator checks formats and ranges (packages/api-client/src/runtime.ts:37-62, 81-140). Fixtures shared with Python test it (packages/api-client/tests/contract.test.ts:8-20). Write replies are the exception (XWEB-01).

strengths.title: Every form control goes through one primitive set
strengths.evidence: No raw input, select or textarea exists outside components/ui (grep over components and app). DS-03's control border, focus and dark fill are defined once, in components/ui/field.tsx:6-11 and app/globals.css:95-101.

strengths.title: One token source, imported unedited
strengths.evidence: app/globals.css:1-5 imports docs/design/luma.css and the one documented extension, then maps the semantic tokens in @theme (globals.css:31-77). The only color literals are the theme preview swatches, and a comment explains them (appearance-control.tsx:10-26).

strengths.title: An explicit server-only boundary
strengths.evidence: lib/bff.ts:1, lib/server-config.ts:1, lib/session.ts:1, lib/service-status.ts:1 and lib/workspace-choice.ts:1 import server-only. The same-origin guard is a pure function with a unit test (lib/request-guard.ts:33-67). When the browser disconnects, only the stream ends, never the run (lib/bff.ts:128-131).

strengths.title: Two well-shaped data hooks to spread
strengths.evidence: useLoaded keeps loading, unavailable and ready as one discriminated union and aborts stale requests (tool-catalog.tsx:156-181). useToolUses pages through results, aborts, and reloads when a version changes; workflow-monitor.tsx:254 reuses it (tool-uses.tsx:101-147).

strengths.title: Lost replies on a paid write are handled correctly
strengths.evidence: ContinueRun keeps its idempotency key until the outcome is known, treats a 5xx response like a lost reply, and blocks re-entry with a pending flag (continue-run.tsx:20-21, 39, 47-50, 68-69, 102). It is the model for every run-creating screen.

strengths.title: State is told in words, with accessible interaction models
strengths.evidence: The words carry the state and a dot only repeats it (badge.tsx:6-7, run-list.tsx:126-146). Tool uses are announced in a live region (tool-uses.tsx:257-261). Search is a combobox with a listbox (search-palette.tsx:139-166). Approvals has a J/K and press-twice keyboard model, and every shortcut ignores text fields through lib/keyboard.ts:2-8.

strengths.title: Label maps keyed by generated unions, where adopted
strengths.evidence: provider-settings-panel.tsx:19-49, readiness.tsx:8-13, keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:20-35, search-palette.tsx:14-19 and run-panel.tsx:22-26 key their maps by generated union types. The compiler therefore flags a state the API adds.

findings.title: Write requests and error bodies bypass the generated contract

locations.note: The POST /api/v1/runs body is an untyped object literal, although RunRequest exists. Line 311 casts the reply to { run_id } instead of using parseRunAccepted.
Casts the admission reply although parseRunAccepted exists.
Casts to { id } although parseSessionView exists. The same cast is at line 144, expert-editor.tsx:201 and goal-composer.tsx:273.
One of 19 hand-cast error bodies. parseErrorResponse has no caller in apps/web; only the api-client contract test calls it.

role_bindings is cast to Record<string, string> because the contract types it as Record<string, unknown>. model-policy-panel.tsx:55 and 130 and experts-panel.tsx:331 cast it the same way, while run-disclosure.tsx:74-79 narrows it with typeof.
Emits path parameters and a JSON body only. Query parameters, such as group, q, profile and cursor on GET /v1/runs, are dropped.
A failed request throws a ContractError with the status in the message and the body discarded. Per-call headers already fit ClientOptions.headers (line 154).

findings.impact: Only half of each exchange is checked. Responses are validated, but requests and refusals are not. RunRequest forbids extra fields (services/agent/src/autobots/contracts/run_commands.py:16), so a renamed field compiles cleanly and fails as a 422 in the browser. The composer reports that 422 as 'That model or request isn't approved' (goal-composer.tsx:331-334). Because the generated functions cannot take query parameters or report a refusal, browser screens cannot use them. The server path (lib/service-status.ts) and the browser path (raw fetch) have therefore diverged.
findings.recommendation: First, type every body with the generated request types (`const body: RunRequest = {...}` or `satisfies`). Replace the 7 success casts with parseRunAccepted and parseSessionView. Read refusals through one readRefusal(reply) helper built on parseErrorResponse, which tolerates non-JSON bodies. Then extend scripts/generate_contracts.py to emit typed query parameters, make runtime.ts throw an ApiError that carries the status and the parsed ErrorResponse, and regenerate. Idempotency-Key can already travel in a per-call ClientOptions.headers; emitting the OpenAPI header parameter as a typed argument is optional. Finally, add lib/api/browser.ts, which binds the generated functions to the /api base, with csrfFetch for writes.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'Use generated API types ... No blanket type assertions to conceal contract mismatches'. contracts.md: 'generated TypeScript consumes them'. The fix changes the generator and runtime.ts and then regenerates generated.ts. It never hand-edits that file (ground rule 2).
findings.verifierNote: Every cited cast, the 28 untyped bodies and the generator's path-and-body-only emission are confirmed. Corrected the success casts to 5 files, noted that 2 bodies target BFF-owned routes, and noted that per-call headers already fit ClientOptions.headers.

findings.title: No shared client data layer: 23 files hand-roll fetch-in-effect

locations.note: The only generic read hook, and it is private to this file.
load() and the initial effect are two copies of the same read. setCounts runs twice at lines 170-171.
The same load-and-effect pair.
The same pair. keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:168-197 repeats it again.
A refetch is triggered by a counter kept in state. run-list.tsx:167 and run-panel.tsx:60 do the same.
Fetches /api/models, and its child RunDisclosure fetches it again on the same mount (run-disclosure.tsx:44-67).
Three requests in one effect. Two of their failures are swallowed with .catch(() => undefined).

findings.impact: Each screen chooses its own flags, abort behavior, body draining and reload trigger. A fix such as aborting stale requests, showing a denied state or offering a retry has to be applied file by file. Sibling components request the same resource independently. Every new screen adds about 25 lines of plumbing, and this plumbing makes up most of the non-JSX code in the largest screens.
findings.recommendation: Generalize useLoaded into hooks/use-resource.ts. It should return one discriminated union (loading, ready with data, denied, or unavailable) plus reload(), with an AbortController and body draining built in. Add hooks for shared reads, such as use-models and use-tool-catalog. Let identical GETs that are in flight at the same time share one request, and keep nothing after it settles, so no data outlives a sign-out (which only calls router.refresh()) or a workspace switch. This needs no new dependency. Migrate panels one at a time and keep their data-* hooks. Pair this with the typed browser client from XWEB-01.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'Represent loading, empty, denied, unavailable and retryable states deliberately', 'Browser state is a view of durable state' and 'Prevent workspace data from leaking through shared caches'. nextjs.md: explicit error, empty and loading states. A read hook is a view only, and no business rule moves into Next.js.
findings.verifierNote: Recounted 28 guarded effects in 23 files, 45 no-store GETs, 60 /api/v1 literals, abort in 2 files and 12 body drains. Narrowed the shared-read cache to in-flight sharing, because sign-out keeps the tab's memory and DH-06 forbids workspace data in shared caches.

findings.title: Writes have no shared submit path, and run admission isn't guarded against a second press

locations.note: Run stays enabled while admission is in flight. run() at 276-341 keeps no pending state.
Comment: one key per press. This is the US-4.1 choice.
The button is disabled only by !ready. run() at 45-80 has no pending flag.
'Run this version' creates an execution with a new key on each press, and the button is never disabled.
The model to follow: a pending flag, and a key kept until the outcome is known (lines 39, 47-50, 69, 102).
Session creation is copied four times: here, at 131-149, at expert-editor.tsx:187-206 and at goal-composer.tsx:257-274.
Its mutate() is copied in keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:203-226, with the same fallback text.
The only write without a catch. A network failure becomes an unhandled rejection, and no message appears.

findings.impact: A double click on Run in the composer, Run in a session, or Run this version sends two admissions with different keys. The API admits two runs and reserves two budgets, which is a paid path. Every write rebuilds headers, keys, its catch style and its refusal reading. A fix in one place, such as the missing catch in Operations, therefore reaches none of the others. Five screens with text inputs submit from onClick buttons without a <form>: goal-composer, session-panel, workflow-editor, the operations retention fields and unknown-effects.
findings.recommendation: Add hooks/use-submit.ts, which owns the following. Pending state that disables the trigger and ignores re-entry. The idempotency-key policy as an explicit option: per-press for the composer as US-4.1 chose, or until-known as ContinueRun does. Unknown-outcome handling for network failures and 5xx responses. A typed outcome union as its result. Route writes through the typed browser client, and add lib/api/sessions.ts with startSession(kind, experts) for the four copies. Wrap writes that have text inputs in a <form>. Start with the three run-creating screens, and add a browser test that double-clicks Run and expects one admission.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'Disable duplicate submits with server idempotency as the correctness mechanism'. The composer keeps one key per press, as decided in openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-05-us-4-1-atomic-run-admission-canonical/proposal.md:10. The recommendation only adds the in-flight guard.
findings.verifierNote: Recounted 29 csrfFetch sites in 19 files, 28 Content-Type literals, 18 randomUUID calls and in-flight guards in 8 files. The three unguarded run buttons and Operations' missing catch are confirmed. Corrected the form count to five, since ContinueRun has no text input.

findings.evidence: In metrics.md section 7, the ten longest non-test functions are all route-level screens: RunWorkspaceView 677, WorkflowEditor 617, GoalComposer 527, ExpertEditor 393, OperationsPanel 377, ModelPolicyPanel 350, WorkflowsPanel 341, ApprovalsPanel 308, RunInspectorView 263 and RunList 260. 83 functions are over 60 lines. In the three largest, state, effects and writes take about 180, 290 and 230 lines before the first JSX.
findings.impact: Changing any section's data or markup means editing a function of 300 to 700 lines. Most of the non-JSX code is the per-screen plumbing described in the two findings above, so every large screen has the same seams. Area reviewers can't fix this one screen at a time without first creating the shared hooks.
findings.recommendation: Split each large screen along three seams: a data hook built on useResource or a stream hook, an actions hook built on useSubmit, and presentational section components, which can be Server Components when they are read-only. Do the splits after the hooks exist, so that each split removes code instead of moving it. Keep every data-* hook the browser suites read.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'small cohesive modules'. The splits must keep the data-* hooks and accessible names that the browser suites assert.
findings.verifierNote: The ten function spans, line counts and complexities match metrics.md section 7. The lines before the first JSX are 181, 292 and 230 in the three largest screens.

findings.title: Model profile names and the offered set are hardcoded in three screens

locations.note: PROFILES lists Terra and Sol and doubles as the offered set.
Bindings outside the list are dropped on save. The UI says so at 424-432 and disables the option at 415-421.
PROFILE_NAMES maps profile IDs to names by hand.
An identical PROFILE_NAMES copy.
Reads `offered` from /api/models instead. goal-composer.tsx:393-395 does the same.
Also reads offered from the server.
OFFERED_FOR_NEW_RUNS, which owns the rule.

findings.evidence:
grep 'openrouter_terra' in apps/web/components finds three hardcoded copies. Only expert-editor's PROFILES encodes the offered rule. The two PROFILE_NAMES maps are display labels, which /api/models doesn't carry: it returns profile, canonical_id and offered. Excerpt from expert-editor.tsx:21-25 and 126-128:
  const PROFILES = [
    { id: "", label: "Workspace setting" },
    { id: "openrouter_terra", label: "Terra" },
    { id: "openrouter_sol", label: "Sol" },
  ];
  const dropped = others
    .filter(([, profile]) => !PROFILES.some((item) => item.id === profile))
findings.impact: Which models new runs may use is a server rule, and /api/models already exposes it. Qualifying Sol (commit ada547a, US-14.15) required a manual edit to this list. The next qualification will need edits in three files. Until they are made, the Expert editor labels a qualified model as not offered and drops its bindings on save, while the composer offers that same model. The maps are typed Record<string, string>, so the compiler doesn't catch a missing profile even though the client exports ModelProfileId.
findings.recommendation: Read profiles from /api/models through one shared hook (useModels) in all three screens. Label them with the server's canonical_id, or keep short names in one lib map typed Record<ModelProfileId, string>. Derive 'not offered' from model.offered, never from a local list.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'Avoid ... duplicated business rules'. nextjs.md: 'Next.js owns UI/BFF, not Python business-state transitions'. The rule stays in the Python domain, and the screens only read it.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed the three copies, OFFERED_FOR_NEW_RUNS at models.py:72 and the manual edit in ada547a. Lowered from high to medium: only one copy encodes the rule, the editor warns before a save drops a binding, and WBLD-07 and XDUP-10 rate the same issue medium.

findings.impact: In three places a user cannot tell a load that is still running from one that failed. Search hides an outage as 'no match'. On most screens, denied cannot be told apart from unavailable. Tests can assert a view state only where the screen added data-state.
findings.recommendation: Add components/ui/view-state.tsx with Loading, Empty, Unavailable (with an optional retry) and Denied. Each sets its role and data-state the same way and is driven by the resource hook's status. Map 401 and 403 to Denied, and network failures and 5xx to Unavailable. Never swallow a secondary load; show a muted unavailable line instead.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'Represent loading, empty, denied, unavailable and retryable states deliberately'. nextjs.md asks for explicit error, empty and loading states. DS-03 lists empty, loading and error states as design-system surfaces.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed the three Loading lines that never clear, search's empty result on failure, four differently styled failure states, and 403 named only by Operations. Recounted 9 swallowed loads in 6 files and about 30 loading lines in 22 files.

The same endpoint's refusals are mapped another way, with no credential_invalid, no budget case and no link to settings.
A third way: it shows the server's message.
The model to follow: refusals as an alert and confirmations as a status note.

findings.evidence:
There are 3 different mappings for POST /api/v1/runs refusals, and owner_required is worded in 8 places across 6 files (grep owner_required in apps/web/components). Excerpt from session-panel.tsx:71-79:
  setProblem(
    failure?.code === "credentials_required"
      ? "Model-backed work needs an OpenRouter key."
      : failure?.code === "model_not_offered"
        ? "A saved model choice isn't offered for new runs until it's qualified, ..."

findings.impact: The same refusal from the same endpoint reads differently on Home, in a session and on a run. Screen readers interrupt for a success on Home, but announce refusals only politely in the editors and on Operations. Every new error code has to be added in several files.
findings.recommendation: Add lib/refusals.ts, which maps ErrorResponse.code (read with parseErrorResponse) to text and an optional action link for each context: admission, owner and version conflict. Add an Outcome component that renders refusals with role=alert and confirmations with role=status, as RunControls already does. Keep the existing wording that the browser suites read.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'centralize error handling ... and expose safe typed errors'.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed the three admission refusal mappings, role=alert on the composer's success, role=status for refusals in the editors and Operations, and owner_required worded at 8 sites in 6 files.

The hand-written TERMINAL and PAUSABLE sets are a second state enum that can drift from the server's transition table. The opposite version policies of RunPanel and RunControls are recorded in US-15.17's design, and each file explains only its own (run-panel.tsx:82, run-controls.tsx:64), so the copied buttons hide that the two differ.
findings.recommendation: Add lib/run-status.ts with labels, sentences and tones typed Record<RunStatus, ...>, and one RunStateBadge used by the list, the panel, the run page, Home and Workflows. Have the API send the allowed commands, as it already sends can_continue (run-workspace.tsx:425), instead of commandsFor's sets. Add one RunCommandButtons component with an explicit versionPolicy prop.

findings.title: Shared vocabulary and hooks live inside feature components, imported sideways and in a cycle

locations.note: Imports RunPanel ...
... and run-panel imports StateLine back from run-list, which makes an import cycle.
A Build screen imports AVAILABILITY and repair() from the 853-line tool catalog.

findings.impact: Pure helpers can only be reached through 'use client' modules, so they cannot be unit-tested without pulling in JSX and the React graph. A change to a list component ripples into Home, Workflows and the Expert editor. The run-list cycle works only because both imports are used inside functions.
findings.recommendation: Move pure vocabulary and formatting into lib/ (run-status, tool-labels, format, refusals) with no React. Put hooks in hooks/ (use-resource, use-submit, use-tool-uses, use-models, use-mounted). Group screens in feature folders (components/runs, home, build, tools, approvals, settings, shell). Add a no-restricted-imports rule that forbids importing another feature folder's internals, allowing only its public entry module, and keep server-only code out of any entry module that client components import.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'explicit ownership, narrow interfaces ... small cohesive modules'. DH-03 places only apps/web/ itself, so folders inside it don't conflict with it.
findings.verifierNote: Recounted 24 feature-to-feature import edges, 7 of them carrying helpers, constants or a hook, and the run-list and run-panel cycle. Reworded the lint rule so a shared entry module can't pull server-only code into a client bundle.

findings.title: Screen state is spread across independent flags where one union belongs
